title: Polymarket bot — operations (paper)
description: WP-240 operations view. Every panel is bound to a metric the control API genuinely exports (packages/observability PLATFORM_METRIC_FAMILIES). PAPER deployment: this dashboard exposes no live-mode control, no run-mode change and no credential.

panels.title: Run mode and ceiling
panels.description: The control API's run mode, its process maximum and the repository ceiling, beside the reported trader's. The ceiling is NOT writable through this API — there is no request that names a run mode — so a change here means a process was restarted with different configuration. control_allow_real_orders is structurally 0.

panels.title: Trader health report available
panels.description: READ THIS FIRST. 0 means the control API holds no trader health report that passed its door, so every trader_* panel below is stale or empty — that is a control-plane fact, not a quiet trading day.

panels.title: Latched halts
panels.description: A halt is a LATCH: once raised, the trader makes no trading decision for the scope until an operator act clears it. trader_healthy is 1 only while no scope is halted.

panels.title: Halt detail
panels.description: One row per latched halt: the §14.1 scope, the reason code that raised it and the §9.9 action it selects. An action is what the process recommends; only the scope-level latch is what it enforces.

panels.title: Queue depth
panels.description: §8.3 bounded queues. Depth approaching the bound is backpressure building; the trader's queues REFUSE at the bound and never drop.

panels.title: Queue oldest message age
panels.description: Age of the oldest queued message. A GAP in this series means the queue was empty — the exporter omits the sample rather than reporting 0, because an empty queue has no oldest message.

panels.title: Queue backpressure
panels.description: Milliseconds producers spent refused at a full queue, plus accepted/consumed totals so the lag can be audited. trader_queue_messages_dropped_total must stay flat at 0; any increase is a contract break, not a load symptom.

panels.title: Seam: fill deduplication
panels.description: The at-most-once gate. trader_seam_fills_evictions_total above 0 means the seam can no longer prove at-most-once for the whole run — the bound is too small, and the number says so rather than hiding it.

panels.title: Seam: inventory reservations
panels.description: WP-220 obligation 9's inventory book. The reserved amount is an EXACT decimal carried as a label on an info gauge; it is displayed, never charted, because a float64 sample value is the representation §6 invariant 1 forbids for economics.

panels.title: Seam: cancels
panels.description: Obligation 10: every cancel reaches a terminal fact. trader_seam_cancels_silence_exceeded_total counts cancels closed by their silence bound — §6 invariant 6 forbids treating that as a rejection.

panels.title: Seam: order views
panels.description: Obligations 4 and 5a. A repeat is LABELLED and delivered, never dropped, so repeats rising is information rather than loss.

panels.title: Seam: capital allocator
panels.description: The §9.7 commitment book behind §9.8 checks 14 and 15. Refusals are broken out by the allocator's own code; the reserved pUSD is an exact decimal carried as a label.

panels.title: Observe-only intents (shadow instances)
panels.description: Intents a NON-OWNER instance emitted that were never routed (§6 invariant 11, ADR-011 §5: a shadow instance submits nothing). A non-zero rate with no fills is the process declining to route what a strategy emitted — not the strategy emitting nothing.

panels.title: Kill switches engaged
panels.description: §14.1 kill switches latched through the control API, by scope and action. Engaging one is an operator act and is audited; so is releasing one, which additionally requires evidence.

panels.title: Strategy instances by run state
panels.description: Instances the control plane knows, by run state, plus one series per instance an operator has paused.

panels.title: Control-plane refusals
panels.description: Authentication failures never reach the control plane and therefore write no audit record; this counter is where they become visible. Authorization failures are authenticated callers lacking an explicit grant (§15). Mode-raise refusals are requests that tried to raise a run mode, enable real orders, raise a live-micro cap or name a signer — each refused by name AND audited.

panels.title: Audit log
panels.description: Acceptance 2 made observable. The control plane audits BEFORE it applies, so control_audit_append_failures_total counts mutations that did NOT happen, and records reaching capacity stops the control plane from mutating anything rather than evicting evidence.

panels.title: Event loop throughput
panels.description: §8.1 core loop. Refused events are events the wire door would not read, or whose instant could not be normalised — a feed or contract problem, not load.

panels.title: Feature engine
panels.description: Snapshots computed, evaluations skipped for want of one, and projection refusals. 'Unavailable' is ordinary early-run state (no book has arrived yet) and is counted separately from a refused event on purpose — merging them would make a healthy start look like a feed problem.

panels.title: Deliveries suppressed by halt
panels.description: Fill and order-view deliveries the §4.2 halt gate withheld from a strategy. The ACCOUNTING for those events still happened — the money moved whatever this process's state is — and this is the other half of that sentence.

panels.title: Input stream lag (entries behind head)
panels.description: THROUGHPUT-1a. Events published to the trader's input stream and not yet delivered to it (the stream head minus the trader's position), sampled every second, against the stream's retention bound. When the lag reaches the bound, retention removes unread events and the trader halts TRANSPORT_RESYNC_REQUIRED (ADR-003 §3.3) — H1 run 1's halt. 'Queue depth' above is the in-process ingest queue and reads 0 however far behind the stream the trader is.

panels.title: Event-time lag
panels.description: THROUGHPUT-1a. Wall clock minus the recorded receivedAt of the last event the trader processed: how far behind the market its decisions are. The sample age says how old the stream positions in 'Input stream lag' are; a growing age means the sampler cannot reach the stream.
